description: #5057 — `start_pairing`, the HOST half of pairing, and the counterpart to `pairing_confirm.json`. It was waived as a 'pairing transport session; no durable domain state to snapshot', and PERMANENTLY so, which is the worse half: the IPC calls `start_pairing_armed`, which makes the same TWO durable writes the joiner does. One is unobservable — the `pending_pairing` marker in `app_settings`, for the reason `cancel_pairing` stays permanently excluded: no command on the IPC surface, on either stack, reads that key, so no query step can see it armed. THIS FIXTURE DOES NOT PIN IT. The other is `clear_unpaired_by_peer_all`, which drops the #4297 'this peer says we are not paired' flag from EVERY `peer_refs` row, and `list_peer_refs` projects that column — so the step below is the observation, exactly as it is for `confirm_pairing` and for the three peer writers in `peer_ref_writes.json`. The mock returned a frozen `{passphrase, qr_svg}` and wrote nothing, so a host that had recorded a peer's refusal kept prompting to re-pair right after arming. The RETURN carries nothing either: the passphrase is minted per stack and the QR derives from it.
name: pairing_start

ops.comment: The host arms pairing. There is no input to get wrong — the passphrase is generated, not typed — so the only thing this op can leave behind is the flag clear below.
ops.name: arm_pairing_on_the_host

queries.comment: The observation: `peer-flagged` has lost its unpaired stamp and every other column is untouched — the clear is scoped to one column, not to one peer, because a host arming a window does not yet know which peer will answer it.
queries.name: peers_after_arming
